title: Promotion evidence
description:
The record a promotion is decided on: one corpus, one corpus ref, two revision sets, the typed-output diff between them, and the approvals for anything the diff found (ADR-046, `REG-016`).

PROMOTION HAPPENS ON EVIDENCE, NEVER ON A VERSION CLAIM. "The upstream change is compatible" is a claim about someone else's estate, and claims about someone else's estate deserve evidence. The evidence exists deterministically — compile the organization's own intent corpus under both revisions and compare what each publishes — so the alternative to producing it is not trust, it is a decision taken with the answer available and unread.

THE DIFF IS THE ENTIRE GATE. Empty, or every entry explicitly approved. Anything else refuses the promotion outright, and nothing partially promotes: a half-promoted estate is one where the pinned and candidate revisions are both live and neither is the answer to "what is this estate running".

AND A NON-EMPTY DIFF IS ALSO A FINDING. It contradicts the upstream compatibility claim, so it routes home with the diff as provenance (`finding-routing-record.schema.json`). The estate that discovered the incompatibility is the one holding the evidence for it, and letting that die locally means the next estate rediscovers it.

corpus_ref.description:
The single ref both compilations ran against — a commit, a tag, a content digest.

ONE REF, RECORDED, AND IT IS AN INVARIANT RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. A corpus that moved between the two compilations makes the diff meaningless: a difference could then be the revision change or the corpus change, and nothing in the artifact distinguishes them. Recording the ref is what makes the evidence re-derivable by someone who did not run it — which is the only kind of evidence worth the name.

from_revisions.description: The revision set the estate is pinned to — what it runs today. Pinned handles in `thing@version` or `thing@sha256:` form.

to_revisions.description: The candidate revision set — what promotion would move it to. A set rather than a single version because a promotion is an estate moving, not an artifact bumping, and the diff is only interpretable against the whole set that produced it.

diff.description:
What the two compilations published differently, compared on DECLARED OUTPUTS ONLY — never provider internals, which are not a contract and would make every provider change look like a breakage.

Outputs the model declares `volatile` are excluded BY THAT DECLARATION (`common-elements` `$defs/volatile_output`), never ad hoc at diff time. An ad-hoc exclusion would let a promotion be waved through by excluding whatever happened to differ.

An empty array is the passing case and must be distinguishable from an absent one — hence required.

output.description: The declared output that differed, by name.

change.description: `removed` and `type_changed` break any consumer bound to the output. `value_changed` on a non-volatile output is the subtler case: the shape held and the realized fact moved — which is exactly what the compatibility claim promised would not happen. `added` is reported rather than ignored, because an output nobody expected is a surface nobody reviewed.

approval.description: The explicit approval for THIS entry. Per-entry, never a blanket sign-off on the diff: approving a list is approving whatever is on it, and the point of the gate is that a human looked at each difference.

volatile_outputs_excluded.description: The outputs left out of the comparison because they declare `volatile: true`. Recorded so the exclusion is auditable: an exclusion nobody can see is indistinguishable from a difference nobody reported.

outcome.description: Derived, and recorded because the record is the artifact somebody reads later: `promoted` iff the diff is empty or every entry carries an approval; `refused` otherwise. `validate.py` recomputes it rather than trusting it — an outcome that disagrees with its own diff is the one failure this record exists to make impossible.

finding_uuid.description: The finding-routing record that carried this diff upstream, where one was filed. A non-empty diff contradicts the upstream compatibility claim, and `REG-016` rules that a refusal which cannot yet file the record QUEUES the filing rather than dropping it — so absence here means not-yet-filed, never not-required.

approval.reason: Estate re-imaged to UEFI in the same window; the new default matches reality.
